evidence.claim: Scholz said antisemitism, hate speech, hate against Israel, and violence against Jews were increasing, insisted that antisemitism has no place in Germany, and warned that free societies must not let extremists take control; he also referred to protesters wearing yellow stars marked 'unvaccinated' as a distortion of Holocaust memory.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz beim Internationalen Gedenktag der Unesco an die Opfer des Holocaust am 27. Januar 2022
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said antisemitism, hate speech, hate against Israel, and violence against Jews were increasing, insisted that antisemitism has no place in Germany, and warned that free societies must not let extremists take control; he also referred to protesters wearing yellow stars marked 'unvaccinated' as a distortion of Holocaust memory.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary contemporaneous Scholz speech; strong direct ruler attribution for incitement and anti-hate posture.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to incitement, minority protection, and crisis rhetoric.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz speech and framing; not inherited context.
contrary_evidence: A speech is not the same as enforcement or remedy.
The source shows stance more than measurable protection outcomes.

evidence.claim: On 4 April 2022 Scholz visited Tegel, which had become a central arrival and registration point for people fleeing Ukraine; the registration process helped refugees obtain accommodation, work permits, and free language courses.
evidence.title: Federal Chancellor Scholz visits arrival centre in Berlin-Tegel
evidence.excerpt: On 4 April 2022 Scholz visited Tegel, which had become a central arrival and registration point for people fleeing Ukraine; the registration process helped refugees obtain accommodation, work permits, and free language courses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government visit note with concrete service details and dated ruler presence.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to refugee protection and domestic crisis management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz's public prioritization of refugee reception, though delivery depended on federal and Land administration.
contrary_evidence: This is a visit and service description, not evidence of nationwide effectiveness.
The underlying refugee influx was inherited from Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

evidence.claim: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome in Germany and that the federal government, Länder, and municipalities would ensure shelter, medical care, schooling, and a safe future; he also announced additional humanitarian support.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz bei der Online-Geberkonferenz 'Stand up for Ukraine'
evidence.excerpt: Scholz said Ukrainian refugees were welcome in Germany and that the federal government, Länder, and municipalities would ensure shelter, medical care, schooling, and a safe future; he also announced additional humanitarian support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary dated Scholz video statement with explicit protection commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 during the refugee-response phase of the Ukraine war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz commitment, though implementation was shared across levels of government.
contrary_evidence: Humanitarian promises do not guarantee actual delivery.
The source concerns refugees from an external war, not ordinary domestic crime.

evidence.claim: The Court found that Germany failed to ensure through an independent body an effective investigation into an arguable racial-profiling allegation involving a federal police identity check, and found the internal investigation insufficiently independent.
evidence.title: BASU v. Germany
evidence.excerpt: The Court found that Germany failed to ensure through an independent body an effective investigation into an arguable racial-profiling allegation involving a federal police identity check, and found the internal investigation insufficiently independent.
evidence.source_locator: HUDOC case description and judgment summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Binding judicial finding from the ECHR; strong independent corroboration of oversight failure.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and highly relevant to policing oversight during the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Germany's law-enforcement and judicial framework during Scholz's term, not a personal order from Scholz.
contrary_evidence: The incident predated Scholz's chancellorship, though the legal failure was judged in 2022.
The case concerns a specific identity check, not the whole policing system.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said some protests were disproportionately restricted, including a June 2022 limit of only 50 demonstrators at the Germany-hosted G7 site.
evidence.title: Deutschland 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said some protests were disproportionately restricted, including a June 2022 limit of only 50 demonstrators at the Germany-hosted G7 site.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights NGO annual report with a concrete restriction example and target-year fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is partly attributable to federal hosting and security policy under Scholz, but the immediate decision was operational and intergovernmental rather than solely personal.
contrary_evidence: A security restriction at a G7 summit is not proof of generalized repression.
The report gives one concrete example rather than a nationwide pattern.

evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that in August 2022 police in Dortmund fatally shot a 16-year-old Senegalese refugee with multiple rounds from a machine gun, and that criminal investigations were still ongoing at year-end.
evidence.title: Deutschland 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reported that in August 2022 police in Dortmund fatally shot a 16-year-old Senegalese refugee with multiple rounds from a machine gun, and that criminal investigations were still ongoing at year-end.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear annual-report documentation of a serious police use-of-force case and ongoing investigation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This was a state-police incident under Scholz's chancellorship, but it was a state-level operational event rather than a federal order.
contrary_evidence: The report does not establish Scholz personally directed the shooting.
This is a single grave event, not by itself evidence of a nationwide terror pattern.

evidence.claim: After the Reichsbürger raids, Scholz said Germany has a resilient state and a militant democracy and that the security authorities can thwart such violations; the raids themselves led to 25 arrests in a far-right coup plot case.
evidence.title: Nach Razzia gegen 'Reichsbürger' Scholz besorgt über Verbindungen zur AfD
evidence.excerpt: After the Reichsbürger raids, Scholz said Germany has a resilient state and a militant democracy and that the security authorities can thwart such violations; the raids themselves led to 25 arrests in a far-right coup plot case.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent reporting with direct Scholz quotation and clear event context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in late 2022 and relevant to crisis response and domestic extremist threats.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz public response to a domestic security threat; the raid was executed by security services rather than personally by him.
contrary_evidence: The quote reflects rhetoric after enforcement, not prior prevention.
The plot was a policing/intelligence success, but the article does not prove Scholz personally ordered it.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that police were doing too little to prevent racism and antisemitism inside the police, noting that police training addressed the issue in only 5 of 16 federal states and that independent complaint bodies existed in only seven states.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Germany
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that police were doing too little to prevent racism and antisemitism inside the police, noting that police training addressed the issue in only 5 of 16 federal states and that independent complaint bodies existed in only seven states.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent annual human-rights review citing a specific study and summarizing structural oversight deficits.
evidence.period_fit: Covers 2022 conditions and provides structural context for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural and multi-level responsibility under the Scholz chancellorship; not a single-person act.
contrary_evidence: The finding is study-based and not a direct audit of federal command.
State-level variation limits direct federal attribution.

unresolved_gaps: No primary record of a Scholz-led command-and-control, custody, or safety reform in 2022.
The strongest direct evidence is signaling and procurement, not measured risk-reduction outcomes.
No private cabinet, NATO, or Russian-channel records showing the full decision chain behind caution, escalation limits, and ceasefire efforts.
No enacted 2022 Scholz-led federal police-oversight, complaint, or anti-racism reform was recovered.
The record is stronger on baseline freedoms, court protection, and limited reforms than on direct Scholz-led 2022 expansion of contestability.
Household-level distribution and long-run productivity effects remain thinner than the policy and macro response record.
Independent 2022 outcome data on take-up, distribution, and durability of the social measures is limited.
No direct, independently verified evidence of personal enrichment, family/business conflict, or nepotism was recovered.
The central Cum-Ex dispute still lacks the original transcript or decision PDF needed to resolve the truthfulness question cleanly.
Direct personnel, delegation, and implementation-discipline evidence is thinner than program, budget, procurement, and outcome evidence.
Some outcome indicators are partly inherited or shock-driven, so causal attribution for 2022 success remains mixed.
